newsitem.title: CANADA: TrizecHahn to issue C$250 mln of debt.
newsitem.headline: TrizecHahn to issue C$250 mln of debt.

text.p: TrizecHahn Corp said on Monday it will issue C$250 million of unsecured five-year debentures in Canada on a bought deal basis to refinance existing debt on the company's Place Ville Marie office complex in Montreal.
TrizecHahn said the debentures will carry a fixed interest rate which will be 70 basis points over the Government of Canada's bond yield when the coupon is set later this week.
Based on the current bond yield, the debentures would have an interest rate of 6.2 percent, significantly lower than the 11 percent debt being replaced.
The transaction will also extend the current debt maturity by three years to 2002 and add to TrizecHahn's pool of unencumbered assets for additional financial flexibility, the company said.

The debentures have been rated B++ by Canadian Bond Rating Service with a positive outlook and BBB (stable) by Dominion Bond Rating Service. The underwriting group consists of Goldman Sachs Canada, Nesbitt Burns Inc, Midland Walwyn Capital Inc and J.P. Morgan Securities Canada Inc.
TrizecHahn said it has filed a preliminary short form prospectus with provincial securities regulators in Canada and that the debentures have not been registered for sale in the United States.
Shares of TrizecHahn fell 0.05 to 29.80 in mid-morning Toronto Stock Exchange trading of more than 30,000 shares.
